datasets.description: Author-released dataset of citations made in patents, including citations to other patents and to scientific literature found in the patent text, linked to patent identifiers.
notes: The concept DOI resolves to the latest Zenodo version, 0.3.1 (December 2020). Two earlier versions exist. The paper reports 49.5 million in-text patent citations; its data statement points to an online appendix that was not read, so which version matches the paper's counts is not verified.

Eight data archives of 6 MB to 4 GB plus a README. The archives are named .tar but are gzip-wrapped and hold gzip-compressed shards, so decompress twice. Only the start of the in-text patent file was read.
A citation_flag column marks citations likely taken from patent headers. The schema advises excluding flagged rows from most analyses.
Zenodo labels the record CC-BY-4.0. The data build on DOCDB/PATSTAT and Google Patents sources, which may carry their own terms.
Different from the Bryan, Ozcan and Sampat database in this library: that one links patents to scientific articles, while the SMJ paper focuses on in-text citations between patents.

links.title: In-text patent citations (CSV shards, 2.8 GB archive)

datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists 9 open files for version 0.3.1 under CC-BY-4.0. A 3 MB range of the in-text patent archive decoded to a schema CSV and the first rows of a data shard (for example US-5728520-A, publication date 19980317, with cited-patent identifiers). Full archives were not downloaded. The project website link was not checked.

datasets.title: U.S. inventor ages, gender and death dates matched to patents
datasets.description: Author-built database matching U.S.-resident patent inventors to estimated birth years, inferred gender and some death dates collected from public web directories, linked to patents by inventor ID.
notes: Personal data warning: the files contain inventor names, city and state of residence, estimated birth years and, for some inventors, death dates, collected from people-search websites. Use only for legitimate research, follow your institution's data-ethics rules, and do not use it to identify or contact individuals.

Quality caveats from the authors: ages come from heuristics and a quality score; death dates are described as less reliable. The checked age file has birth years from 1800 to 2013, so apply plausibility filters.

Twenty-three public files, 3 MB to 1.9 GB. The key files are the inventor age and gender table (2,408,326 rows; 1,858,516 unique inventors), a patent-to-inventor crosswalk (8,080,135 rows, grant years 1976 to 2018) and a death-date table. Other files were listed but not read.
Gender is inferred from first name and birth year by an algorithm; 571,074 rows are marked unknown.
The Dataverse record is marked CC0 1.0. Source websites for the scraped information may have their own terms.
A companion data paper (Kaltenberg, Jaffe and Lachman, “The Age of Invention”, NBER working paper 28768) documents the database.

links.title: Inventor ages, scores and gender (CSV, 198 MB)

datasets.verification: Dataverse API lists 23 public files under CC0 1.0 (version 1.1, May 2021). datasets.title: Open source projects: write access, novelty and survival (replication data)
datasets.description: Author replication package with project-month data on open source repositories, measures of contribution novelty, contributor diversity and survival, plus Stata code and the training data for the novelty classifier.
notes: Complete analysis data and Stata code for the paper's main tables, according to the deposit. The code that built the data from GitHub and the classifier code are not listed in the deposit; the training data and test results are.

Files: a project-month panel (45,418 rows, 6,277 repositories, months 1 to 12), a survival table (6,563 rows), classifier training data (759 rows) and test data (190 rows). CSV files use semicolons as separators.
Repository names and owner handles appear in the panel. They are public GitHub identifiers, but treat them as personal data in publications.
DataverseNL labels the record GNU GPL v3.0, a software license, applied here to data as well. Confirm reuse terms with the authors.
Novelty scores come from a classifier trained on hand-coded commits, so measurement error is part of the data.

datasets.title: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
datasets.description: National survey for adults and children with various health-related questions
notes: Existing library entry enriched with a verified research citation and tags on 16 October 2026.

The cited Management Science paper uses the 2011-2012 cycle for its first study: serum total testosterone and work-situation questions for adults. Its other studies use different data, including the Understanding Society Innovation Panel, which is not part of this entry.
Checked files are the 2011-2012 testosterone (TST_G), occupation (OCQ_G) and demographics (DEMO_G) SAS transport files. NHANES publishes other cycles and many other files.
Older CDC download links (the Nchs/Nhanes/2011-2012 path) now return an HTML 'page not found' with status 200. Use the Data/Nhanes/Public path linked here.
datasets.verification: The three CDC files downloaded as SAS transport and parsed: TST_G has 7,821 respondents (6,826 with a testosterone value), OCQ_G has 6,175 respondents with a work-situation item (OCQ260), DEMO_G has 9,756 respondents and covers every TST_G respondent. The paper's abstract explicitly names NHANES 2011-2012.

datasets.title: U.S. patent secrecy orders in World War II
datasets.description: Author-compiled list of U.S. patent applications placed under secrecy orders in the Second World War era, with filing dates, serial numbers and, where granted, patent numbers for linking to other patent data.
notes: One data table (8,475 secrecy-order records) and a README. 6,353 records have a patent number and grant date; the rest were not matched to a granted patent.
The table has five columns: filing date, serial number, secrecy determination, patent number and grant date. All rows carry the same determination value, 'Secrecy Recommended'.
Compiled from War Department and Office of Scientific Research and Development records held at the U.S. National Archives; the README gives the finding aids.
Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). The README asks users to cite the paper. Patent numbers link to USPTO data such as PatentsView, which is already listed.
datasets.verification: Dataverse API lists two public files under CC BY-NC 4.0. Both were downloaded: the table parsed to 8,475 rows and 5 columns (filing dates 1932-05-09 to 1945-10-15; grant dates 1940-06-18 to 1976-11-09) and the README was read.

datasets.title: Inventors, firms and patent output (replication archive)
datasets.description: Author replication archive linking U.S. patents and inventors to publicly listed firms, with citation measures, inventor employment spells, firm financial variables, Stata code and bootstrap results.
notes: 25 public files, about 2.9 GB. The largest is the inventor-patent file at 1.9 GB. Includes Stata code (a master script runs the analysis in order), MATLAB files and a README listing every variable.

The README says some source files, for example full Compustat data, cannot be shared publicly. The archive contains Compustat-derived files; the authors' record says the files and code replicate the paper's results, but check which inputs are partial before assuming a full rebuild.
Personal data: the LinkedIn match file (23,703 rows) contains inventor names with employer names and employment dates. Handle in line with research ethics rules.
Underlying patent data derive from the NBER patent files (already listed). Compustat terms may restrict reuse of the financial variables. The repository labels the record CC-BY-4.0.
Bootstrapped results may not replicate exactly because of random resampling, according to the authors.
datasets.verification: DataverseNL API lists 25 public files under CC-BY-4.0 (version 1.0, August 2025; the original Erasmus repository DOI forwards here). The README was read in full. Small files were downloaded and parsed (LinkedIn matches 23,703 rows, ownership changes 1,728 rows, a price-deflator table, the master script). Range requests on the three largest Stata files returned HTTP 206 with the Stata file signature. Full large files were not downloaded.

datasets.title: Kickstarter relational database (CrowdBerkeley)
datasets.description: Author-built SQLite database of Kickstarter crowdfunding projects, creators, funders, comments, rewards, locations and funding trends, collected from the public platform.
notes: One database in a split ZIP archive: a 2 GB part and a 1.4 GB part (about 3.5 GB compressed). Download both parts into one folder before unzipping.

Checked content: the archive holds a single file, hdd/kickstarter.db. The start of it was decompressed and is a SQLite database with tables including project, creator, comments, reward, funding_trend and location. The full database was not downloaded.
Personal-data note: platform creator profiles and comment text are included. Use within research ethics rules and platform terms.
The paper presents three databases (Kickstarter, Kiva, CrowdRise). Only the Kickstarter database was found in a public repository; the other two were not located.

The Dataverse record is marked CC0 1.0 (version 2.0, January 2019). The data were scraped from Kickstarter, whose own terms may apply. Collection dates and coverage years are not stated in the record, so they are left unspecified here.
A different library entry, Kickstarter visual features, covers processed image and text features from another study.
datasets.verification: Dataverse API lists two public files under CC0 1.0. Range requests returned HTTP 206: the first part carries the split-archive signature and its start inflates to a SQLite 3 database header with the table names above; the second part's central directory lists the single file hdd/kickstarter.db. Complete files were not downloaded.

datasets.title: Deskilling technology and ride-hail labor supply (replication data)
datasets.description: Author replication package with participant-level data from a vignette experiment and a field experiment on how navigation technology affects ride-hail drivers' willingness to work, with Stata code.
notes: Complete analysis data and Stata code for the paper's tables and figures, according to the deposited README. Stata 18 and the reghdfe, twoway_parea and ppmlhdfe packages are listed as requirements.
Vignette experiment: 26,499 choice rows from 803 participants. Field experiment: 200 rows from 50 participants. A small bootstrap-results table is also included (11 rows).
Participant-level data with de-identified IDs, including age and sex. The country or city of the ride-hail drivers is not stated in the files I read, so geography is left unspecified.
The README lists the data as .dta files; Dataverse serves converted tab-separated copies. The record is marked CC0 1.0 (version 2.0, October 2025).
datasets.verification: Dataverse API lists nine public files under CC0 1.0. The README, main script, bootstrap table, field experiment table (200 rows, 140 columns) and vignette table (26,499 rows, 32 columns) were downloaded and parsed.

datasets.title: Panel Study of Entrepreneurial Dynamics (PSED)
datasets.description: Longitudinal surveys that follow nationally representative samples of people starting businesses in the United States, with data on start-up activities, resources, networks and whether the venture emerges.
notes: Two cohorts: PSED I (screening 1998-2000, 830 nascent entrepreneurs, three follow-ups) and PSED II (screening 2005-2006, six yearly interviews), plus harmonized outcome files that combine them, according to the project site.

The PSED project site states that the data, including restricted geographic data, are distributed through ICPSR. ICPSR downloads need a free account; the restricted geographic data have extra conditions.

The cited papers state in their abstracts that they use PSED I, PSED II or the harmonized files. One cited paper is a replication study of PSED-based work and reports that only some replications succeeded; treat results from this survey with that in mind.
Not verified: ICPSR blocks scripted access, so the data files themselves were not opened for this entry. The ICPSR studies were confirmed through their DOI records, not by download.

datasets.title: Kauffman Firm Survey (public-use microdata)
datasets.description: Panel survey of 4,928 U.S. businesses founded in 2004 and followed through 2011, covering strategy, financing, employment and founder characteristics of new firms.
notes: Public-use microdata in SAS, SPSS and Stata formats, from the baseline (2004) to the seventh follow-up (2011), plus a Stata version with logically imputed values in wide and long format.

More detailed confidential data (finer industry and location codes) are available only through the paid NORC Data Enclave. Some papers use that restricted version, for example a Management Science paper on minority-owned start-ups and a Review of Financial Studies paper on capital structure. They are not cited here because they did not use the public files.
The cited papers state in their abstracts that they use the Kauffman Firm Survey but do not say whether it was the public-use or the restricted version. Check before comparing results.
The Stata public-use file name has dashes; SAS users must remove them, according to the foundation's page.

datasets.title: World Bank Enterprise Surveys
datasets.description: Firm-level surveys of managers and owners in emerging and developing economies on the business environment, innovation, finance, workforce and performance, with matching economy-level indicators.
notes: The Microdata Library lists 794 Enterprise Surveys studies, from country surveys to topical follow-ups such as the Innovation Follow-Up Surveys and a 2026 artificial intelligence follow-up (India).
Firm-level microdata need a free login on the Enterprise Surveys portal; economy-level indicators are shown without one. Users must cite the dataset in the form the World Bank gives for each study.
Most surveys are repeated cross-sections of different firms; a smaller set of panel data exists, according to the program. The cited papers use pooled or merged survey rounds.
Not verified: microdata files sit behind the login, so no data file was opened for this entry. The public sampling methodology note (a PDF) and the catalog records were checked instead.

datasets.title: Reliance on Science — patent-to-paper citations
datasets.description: Author-released data linking patents to the scientific articles they cite, with confidence scores and whether the reference is on the front page or in the text, plus patent-paper pairs.
notes: The Zenodo concept DOI points to the latest of 64 versions. The two latest releases hold only U.S. patents, according to the record, 'in contrast to earlier releases'. The SMJ article studies worldwide front-page citations, so its data correspond to older versions; those were not inspected and the version used in the paper is not verified.

Latest release files: the citation table (1.44 GB; columns include reference type, confidence score, an article identifier named oaid, patent number and where the reference was found), a patent-paper-pairs table (59,202 rows: article id, patent id, confidence level) and a PDF describing the pairs.

Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); the authors ask to be contacted about commercial use. The record asks users to cite the SMJ article, a Journal of Economics and Management Strategy article and a patent-paper-pairs paper.
Citation counts and linking rely on automated extraction and matching, so errors remain; the confidence score helps filter.
datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists three open files in the latest release under CC BY-NC 4.0. The pairs table was downloaded and parsed (59,202 rows, 3 columns). The first rows of the citation table were read by range request. Earlier versions were listed (64 in all) but not opened.

datasets.title: Defense SBIR/STTR awards linked to patents and commercialization
datasets.description: Author-built database linking U.S. Department of Defense small business research awards to the utility patents they produced and to web pages that signal commercialization.
notes: Covers Department of Defense SBIR and STTR awards only, not other agencies. Award data come from the Defense Contract Action Data System (1984-2001) and USAspending.gov (2001-2018); patent data mainly from PatentsView, with details from the Patent Examination Research Dataset or PATSTAT; web pages were collected by the authors' crawls.
Ten small tables (under 5 MB each), including awards (2,213 rows), patents (42,342), award-to-patent links (3,623), web pages (2,027) and legal entities (9,902), plus a README and a schema diagram.
Version 1.1 (August 2025). The record lists the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license and a copyright notice for the authors. The web page table holds addresses and dates, not page content.
This is a derived research database, not the official SBIR.gov award files.
datasets.verification: Zenodo API lists 12 open files. Five tables and the README were downloaded and parsed (row counts above). The remaining tables were listed, not read.

The record states that the R script replicates all figures and tables of the paper. The script and the large files were not run.

datasets.title: Firms in technological space (topological analysis) — replication package
datasets.description: Author replication package with firm-level patent counts by technology area and year, the code to map firms in technology space, and regression data combining the map statistics with firm financial variables.
notes: Includes 30 yearly CSV files of R&D, M&A and combined patent counts by firm and technology area, Python code for the topological (Mapper) analysis, Stata regression code and the data for the main regressions, a README and the draft paper with its online appendix.

Patent data are the first author's compilation of USPTO patents granted 1976-2010, combined with Securities Data Company merger data. Firm financial variables from Compustat (1976-2005) enter only in the regression file; the authors state they have permission to publish their derived outputs, but Compustat is a licensed source, so check its terms.
Licensed CC BY 4.0; the Python code is also on the author's GitHub page under GPL-3.0 according to the README.
Runtime for the main outputs is under 10 minutes on a desktop according to the README. Nothing was run for this entry.

Company names and platform profile links appear in the study 1 table; they come from public start-up profiles but may be sensitive in publications.

The record describes the two studies' datasets as XLSX files, one per study, plus scripts for descriptives and analyses and a folder of custom functions.

datasets.title: Mannheim Innovation Panel (MIP), German innovation survey
datasets.description: Annual representative survey of the innovation activities of German firms (new products and processes, innovation spending, returns), the German part of the Community Innovation Surveys, available to researchers as anonymised scientific use files.
notes: Not freely downloadable. The ZEW Research Data Centre offers on-site use, time-limited remote access, an anonymised scientific use file for non-commercial research and, for some MIP data, an education use file. Scientific use is limited to researchers at publicly funded research institutions, according to ZEW and the DataCite record's rights statement.

The survey has run annually since 1993 and is a panel of firms in mining, manufacturing, energy, construction and business-related and distribution services, according to the DataCite description. The scientific use files in the DOI records cover 1993 to 2016 (one earlier release 1993 to 2014).

The eight Research Policy papers cited are those the data provider's own DOI records list as documenting publications; which version of the MIP data each paper used (scientific use, on-site or earlier releases) is not stated in the record. Their full texts were not read.
Not verified: no data file was opened. ZEW's pages and DOI records were checked; the files need an application to the ZEW Research Data Centre.
datasets.verification: ZEW's MIP page and Research Data Centre page were read and confirm the annual survey since 1993, scientific use files and the access routes. datasets.title: Community Innovation Survey (Eurostat published tables)
datasets.description: European survey of business innovation, run every two years, with Eurostat's free aggregate tables on innovation activity, spending, cooperation and turnover by country, industry and firm size.
notes: The public component is Eurostat's aggregate tables. The catalogue lists ten waves, CIS2006 to CIS2024 (263 tables in all), by country, industry (NACE) and size class, and some by region. Tables are free to download through the Eurostat API.

The cited papers use CIS firm-level microdata (several national, one from Eurostat), not these tables. Table codes follow the pattern inn_cis<n>_*; for example inn_cis13 is CIS2022. Questions and definitions changed over waves, so check the methodology page before comparing waves.
